question.text: Front-running in the context of derivatives trading means:

answer.text: A broker or dealer trading ahead of a large client order to profit from the expected price impact of that order
Placing orders at the front of the order book queue
Being the first to trade when the market opens
Placing stop-loss orders to protect positions

explanation.text: The Logic: Front-running is the practice of a broker, dealer or other intermediary, who has non-public knowledge of a pending large client order that is expected to move the market, placing their own (or related) trades ahead of that client order to capture the resulting price movement. It is a breach of fiduciary duty owed to the client and is treated as a fraudulent and unfair trade practice in Indian securities regulation. The Trap: Front-running is unrelated to literal order-book queue position, has nothing to do with being the first to trade at market open, and is not the same as placing protective stop-loss orders. The defining feature is misuse of advance knowledge of a client order. Note: A direct definition of front-running is not present in the cited pages of the NISM-Series-VIII Equity Derivatives workbook, which on the pages checked covers SEBI powers, broker regulation and grievance mechanisms but not front-running specifically. The framing above is general SEBI PFUTP / market-abuse regulatory knowledge.
